All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
ActiveSigningKeyUseCase
Use case that finds the one key that signs new tokens.
ChangePasswordUseCase
Use case that lets a signed-in user choose a new password.
CheckSecondFactorLockoutUseCase
Use case that tells whether the second factor of a user is locked after too many failed attempts.
CleanExpiredAccountTokensUseCase
Use case that deletes the account tokens (password reset links) that have expired, used or not: once expired they can never be consumed, so keeping them only grows the table.
CleanExpiredAuthorizationsUseCase
Use case that deletes the authorizations whose tokens have all expired, and the abandoned ones: authorization or consent requests that never got a token and are older than a threshold.
CleanExpiredTrustedDevicesUseCase
Use case that deletes the trusted devices that have expired, since they can never be used again.
CleanupOttUseCase
Deletes what the one-time-code and SMS features leave behind: expired codes, expired pending phone verifications, cost ledger rows older than the retention and expired magic-link tokens.
ClientSecretGenerator
Generates random client secrets.
ClockConfiguration
Provides the Clock the use cases read the current time from, so tests can replace it with a fixed one.
ConfirmPhoneUseCase
Confirms a phone with the code that was sent to it.
ConfirmTotpAtSignInUseCase
Use case that confirms the enrolment of an authenticator app inside the sign-in, where the code also stands as the second factor of that sign-in: like VerifyTotpUseCase, a locked second factor is refused, a wrong code counts towards the lockout and a right one clears the counter and is audited.
ConfirmTotpUseCase
Use case that finishes the enrolment of an authenticator app with the first code it shows.
CountRecoveryCodesUseCase
Use case that counts the recovery codes a user still has, so the UI can warn when few are left.
CreateClientUseCase
Use case that registers a client.
CreatedClient
The result of creating a client.
CreatedTrustedDevice
A trusted device just created, with the signed cookie value that is only available now.
CreateTrustedDeviceUseCase
Use case that trusts the browser of a user for some days so it skips the second factor.
DefaultClientDefinitions
The single definition of the clients a deployment can start with: the confidential bff (backend for frontend) and the public spa-public.
DeleteClientUseCase
Use case that deletes a registered client.
DeletePasskeyUseCase
Use case that deletes a passkey of a user and audits the removal.
DeliverOneTimeTokenUseCase
Delivers what the one-time token use cases asked for: an e-mailed code or link, or a text message whose cost was already recorded.
DisableTotpUseCase
Use case that removes the authenticator app of a user together with the recovery codes that went with it.
EmailCodeRequested
Event published when a one-time code must be e-mailed.
EmailLinkRequested
Event published when a magic link must be e-mailed.
EnrollTotpUseCase
Use case that starts the enrolment of an authenticator app: it generates a secret, stores it encrypted and unconfirmed (replacing any earlier unconfirmed one) and returns the otpauth:// URI to show as a QR code.
FindTrustedDeviceUseCase
Use case that finds the usable (not revoked, not expired) trusted device of a user from the value of the cookie.
FindUserAccountUseCase
Use case that looks a user account up by username.
FindUserPhoneUseCase
Finds the verified phone of a user, which the account API shows masked.
GenerateRecoveryCodesUseCase
Use case that creates a fresh set of recovery codes for a user, replacing any previous set.
GetClientUseCase
Use case that looks a client up by its identifier.
HasConfirmedPasskeyUseCase
Use case that tells whether a user has registered a passkey.
HasConfirmedSecondFactorUseCase
Use case that tells whether a user has confirmed any second factor, asking every SecondFactorEnrolmentQuery bean.
HasVerifiedPhoneUseCase
Tells whether a user has a verified phone.
InvalidPhoneNumberException
Thrown when the text typed as a phone number is not a valid number.
IsClientMfaRequiredUseCase
Use case that tells whether a client makes multi-factor authentication mandatory for every user signing in through it (ClientRegistration.mfaRequired()).
IsTotpEnabledUseCase
Use case that tells whether a user has a confirmed authenticator app.
IsUserMfaRequiredUseCase
Use case that tells whether the account of a user requires a second factor, whatever the client being served: when an administrator forced it (users.mfa_required) or when the user has confirmed a second factor (asked to HasConfirmedSecondFactorUseCase), since a factor the user enrolled must protect every sign-in.
ListClientsUseCase
Use case that lists every registered client.
ListPasskeysUseCase
Use case that lists the passkeys of a user.
ListSigningKeysUseCase
Use case that lists every stored signing key, whatever its state, for administration.
ListTrustedDevicesUseCase
Use case that lists the trusted devices of a user that have not expired.
MfaConfiguration
Exposes the domain collaborators of the multi-factor use cases as beans, so no use case creates them and a deployment (or a test) can replace any of them, and binds the MfaProperties.
MfaProperties
Multi-factor settings, bound once from authserver.mfa.* and injected wherever one of them is needed (the use cases of this module and the step-up guard of the API).
OneTimeCodeRequestResult
Outcome of a request for a one-time code.
OttCleanupResult
Number of rows removed by a cleanup run.
OttConfiguration
Declares the collaborators of the one-time-code use cases as beans, so they can be replaced and mocked.
OttDestination
Where a one-time code of a user is delivered.
OttProperties
Settings of the one-time codes, bound from authserver.ott.* once and validated at startup.
OttVerificationResult
Outcome of the verification of a one-time code.
OttVerificationResult.Status
What happened when a code was verified.
PasskeyConfiguration
Binds the PasskeyProperties.
PasskeyProperties
Relying party settings of the passkeys (WebAuthn), bound once from authserver.passkeys.* and injected wherever one of them is needed.
PasswordPolicyConfiguration
Exposes the domain's PasswordPolicy as a bean, so the use cases that check a new password depend on the policy instead of creating it, and a deployment can replace it with a policy of its own.
PhoneEnrolmentStarted
Outcome of starting a phone enrolment.
PublishedSigningKeysUseCase
Use case that finds the keys to publish in the JWKS: the active key, the next key (so relying parties can cache it before it signs) and every retired key whose tokens may still be unexpired.
RecordSecurityEventUseCase
Use case that records a security event (login, second factor, lockout, trusted device) in the audit log.
RecoveryCodes
Creates recovery codes (Crockford base-32 alphabet, so no I, L, O or U) and normalizes what a user types back into that form.
RegisterAccountUseCase
Use case that registers an account.
RegisterSecondFactorFailureUseCase
Use case that counts a failed second-factor attempt and locks the second factor of the user once authserver.mfa.max-failed-attempts consecutive failures are reached.
RemovePhoneUseCase
Removes the phone of a user, verified and pending.
RenamePasskeyUseCase
Use case that renames a passkey of a user.
RequestMagicLinkUseCase
Sends a magic link to the verified e-mail address of an enabled account.
RequestOneTimeCodeUseCase
Sends a one-time code to a user, by e-mail or SMS.
RequestPasswordResetUseCase
Use case that starts a password reset.
ResetPasswordUseCase
Use case that chooses a new password with the single-use token received by e-mail.
ResetSecondFactorFailuresUseCase
Use case that clears the failed second-factor attempts of a user, after a successful verification.
ResolveOttDestinationUseCase
Finds where a one-time code of a user may be delivered: the verified e-mail address or the verified phone of an enabled account.
RevokeTrustedDeviceUseCase
Use case that revokes a trusted device of a user, so it asks for the second factor again.
RevokeUserAuthorizationsUseCase
Use case that revokes every token of a user, for example after a password change or reset.
RotateClientSecretUseCase
Use case that replaces the secret of a confidential client with a new generated one.
RotateSigningKeysUseCase
Use case that keeps the signing keys rotating.
SecondFactorEnrolmentQuery
Extension point that tells whether a user has confirmed one kind of second factor.
SecureRandomOneTimeCodeGenerator
Generates numeric one-time codes with a cryptographically strong random number generator.
SeedRegisteredClientsUseCase
Use case that registers the configured clients (built from DefaultClientDefinitions) that are missing.
SeedResult
Outcome of seeding the default clients.
SendSmsOneTimeCodeUseCase
Requests an SMS inside the cost policy: the country must be served and the spending of the window and of the day, including this message, must stay within their caps.
Sha256OneTimeCodeHasher
Hashes one-time codes with SHA-256 (lower-case hex) and compares them in constant time.
SigningKeyRetention
Decides how long a retired signing key stays published.
SigningKeysRotatedEvent
Published after the signing keys have been rotated, so adapters that cache keys can drop what they hold.
SmsBudgetExceededException
Thrown when an SMS is not sent because it would exceed the spending cap of the window or of the day.
SmsConfiguration
Declares the policy of the SMS channel as a bean.
SmsCountryNotAllowedException
Thrown when an SMS is not sent because its country is not served, or cannot be determined.
SmsMessages
Texts of the SMS messages.
SmsProperties
Settings of the SMS channel, bound from authserver.sms.* once and validated at startup.
SmsRefusedException
Base of the reasons why an SMS is refused before it is sent.
SmsRequested
Event published when a text message, whose cost is already recorded within the budget, must be sent.
StartPhoneEnrolmentUseCase
Starts the enrolment of a phone: normalises the number and sends it a verification code.
TrustedDeviceTokens
Creates the random tokens that identify a trusted device and hashes them, so only the SHA-256 hash is ever stored.
UpdateClientUseCase
Use case that replaces the settings of a registered client; its secret is kept.
UpgradePasswordHashUseCase
Use case that replaces the stored password hash of a user with one made by the current algorithm, right after a successful sign-in (the only moment the clear-text password is known).
VerifyEmailUseCase
Use case that confirms an e-mail address from the signed token that was mailed to it, which also enables the account.
VerifyOneTimeCodeUseCase
Verifies a one-time code.
VerifyRecoveryCodeUseCase
Use case that accepts a recovery code as a second factor.
VerifyTotpUseCase
Use case that verifies a TOTP code presented as a second factor: ±1 step window, no replay of a step already used, lockout after repeated failures, and an audit event either way.
